description: Deliver a one-command copy-paste quickstart via the matrix CLI so users can copy a command and start immediately, AND add click-to-copy command snippets on the website. Depends on FEAT-002 (genesis funding path).
steps: CLI quickstart: add a `matrix quickstart` command in internal/cli that runs a real zero-to-first-job flow against a local node with sensible defaults. It should: ensure/create a local wallet (reuse wallet.go createWallet/loadWallet), then drive the node to (a) fund the wallet account from the reward pool via the FundAccount RPC from FEAT-002, (b) register a demo provider, (c) submit a demo job, and (d) complete/settle it, printing each step and the resulting balances. It must work against a node started with `matrixd --init && matrixd` (dev config from FEAT-002). Keep flags minimal (--addr, reuse globals); print a clear success summary. Alternatively/additionally, if a node-embedded convenience is cleaner, implement `matrix init` to write a dev config, but the copy-paste flow MUST genuinely run end to end.

Document the exact copy-paste one-liner/block in services/core/cmd/matrix/README.md and (later) reference from web. The block should be something a user can paste to go from zero to a funded account / first job, leveraging matrixd --init + matrixd + matrix quickstart.
Add an in-process cli test for `matrix quickstart` against an in-memory MarketService (following internal/cli/integration_test.go), asserting the funded balance and completed job.

Web copy-to-clipboard: create a client component apps/web/src/components/CopyButton.tsx ('use client') that copies a given command string to navigator.clipboard and shows copied feedback (a small button/icon; may use existing sonner toast if convenient, but keep it self-contained and accurate). Keep it a client component; do not touch the @config directive in src/styles/globals.css.

Use CopyButton on the CLI product page apps/web/src/app/products/cli/page.tsx (the existing terminal snippet block) so each start command is click-to-copy, and on the home page apps/web/src/app/page.tsx (a quickstart command near the hero/CTA). Keep the shown commands ACCURATE to what the CLI actually supports after FEAT-002/003 (e.g. matrixd --init; matrixd; matrix quickstart; matrix fund; matrix provider register; matrix job submit).

Optionally add a small quickstart snippet to the marketplace or a quickstart section, but at minimum home + /products/cli must have click-to-copy start commands. If a NEW route/page is added, note it for the orchestrator to screenshot.

Verify Go: make proto && cd services/core && go build ./... && go test ./... (and -race on internal/cli). Verify web: cd apps/web && corepack yarn install --frozen-lockfile && corepack yarn lint && corepack yarn build.
Append the live quickstart transcript (running matrix quickstart against a live node) to .agents/tasks/task-genesis-funding-quickstart/live-loop-transcript.txt or a quickstart-transcript.txt.

corepack yarn lint and corepack yarn build pass for apps/web; go build/test (and -race on internal/cli) pass.
Commands shown on the site match commands the CLI actually supports.
verification: make proto && cd services/core && go build ./... && go test ./... && go test -race ./internal/cli/...
cd apps/web && corepack yarn install --frozen-lockfile && corepack yarn lint && corepack yarn build
Run `matrix quickstart` against a live matrixd and capture the transcript
findings:
Implemented and verified end to end. Committed as b2670e0 (app/library code to main per orchestrator policy; .agents/ task metadata left untracked, matching FEAT-001/002 convention).

WHAT THE QUICKSTART DOES:
- New `matrix quickstart` command (internal/cli/quickstart.go, wired into NewRootCommand in root.go). It runs the whole zero-to-first-job loop against a local node using the SAME market RPCs as the individual subcommands: (1) load-or-create the local wallet at ~/.matrix/wallet.json (reuses wallet.go loadWallet/createWallet; the buyer account), (2) FundAccount to move reward-pool MATRIX to the buyer (the FEAT-002 path; nothing minted), (3) RegisterProvider for a demo provider, (4) SubmitJob (buyer buys units at the provider price), (5) CompleteJob to settle buyer -> provider, then reads GetBalance for both and prints a summary. Each step prints as it runs so the output doubles as a transcript. Flags: --addr/--api-key/--timeout/--json (globals) plus --wallet, --provider, --fund, --capacity, --price, --units (all defaulted). Re-running is idempotent (wallet reused, provider re-registered). Settlement path exercised = market CompleteJob (direct ledger transfer), the sanctioned single-dev-node path, same as FEAT-002.

EXACT COPY-PASTE BLOCK (documented in services/core/cmd/matrix/README.md new 'Quickstart' section, and shown click-to-copy on the site). From services/core:
  go build -o matrixd ./cmd/matrixd && go build -o matrix ./cmd/matrix
  ./matrixd --init && ./matrixd &
  ./matrix quickstart
(For a local dev node the README also notes flipping enable_acls to false so the market API is open; with ACLs on, set MATRIX_ADMIN_API_KEY and pass --api-key.)

listen_addr DEFAULT FIX (the prerequisite so the one-liner genuinely boots): did BOTH robust fixes. (a) internal/node.Initialize now writes network.listen_addr as a full multiaddr '/ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/9000' instead of the bare '0.0.0.0:9000' that broke p2p host init. (b) internal/p2p/host.go now robustly resolves the listen address via a new listenMultiaddr() helper that accepts three forms: empty -> /ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/0; a full multiaddr (starts with '/') used verbatim; and a plain host:port (net.SplitHostPort + ip4/ip6/dns detection) rebuilt into a proper /proto/host/tcp/port multiaddr. So both the new multiaddr default AND any existing host:port configs boot. Added internal/p2p/host_test.go (table test over all address forms incl. ipv6/dns/bare-port/garbage, plus two tests that New() actually boots a libp2p host from a host:port and from a multiaddr). VERIFIED LIVE: a fresh `matrixd --init && matrixd` from the default config now boots and serves (health SERVING), which it did not before.

TESTS ADDED (all pass, incl -race): internal/cli/quickstart_test.go (TestCLI_Quickstart drives the full loop in-process against an in-memory MarketService backed by a real Treasury reward pool, asserts each printed step and the on-ledger balances: buyer 1000 -> 950, provider 0 -> 50 for a 10u@5 job; TestCLI_QuickstartReusesWallet asserts idempotent wallet reuse on a second run). internal/p2p/host_test.go as above.

VERIFICATION RUN: make proto OK; cd services/core && go build ./... OK; go vet ./... OK; go test ./... all OK; go test -race ./internal/cli/... ./internal/p2p/... ./internal/node/... all OK. apps/web: corepack yarn install --frozen-lockfile OK; corepack yarn lint clean (No ESLint warnings or errors); corepack yarn build clean (all 22 routes prerendered). Did NOT touch the @config directive in globals.css.

LIVE TRANSCRIPT: .agents/tasks/task-genesis-funding-quickstart/quickstart-transcript.txt captures a real run: built binaries, `matrixd --init` (default genesis reward_pool 1e18), started matrixd from the default config (only enable_acls flipped to false), `matrix health` SERVING, then `matrix quickstart` funded the buyer 1,000,000, registered quickstart-provider (100 @ 5), submitted+completed a 10u=50 job; independent balance read-back proved buyer 999950 / provider 50 / reward-pool 999999999999000000. Ran as a single self-contained script (build+init+start+CLI loop+kill) because the sandbox isolates each bash call's PID namespace (per FEAT-002 findings). The temp script/dir were removed after capture.
